title: Oppositely transformed matrices can be made hollow and almost hollow
statement:
Let $A,B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ satisfy

$$
\operatorname{trace} A=\operatorname{trace} B=0.
$$

A matrix is **hollow** if all its diagonal entries are zero, and **almost hollow** if it has the corresponding property defined earlier in the paper. The transformations considered below act oppositely on the two matrices.

**Hollowisation conjecture.** There exists an orthogonal matrix $V\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ such that $V^TAV$ is hollow and $VBV^T$ is almost hollow.

Here the transformation applied to $A$ is the inverse, equivalently the adjoint, of the transformation applied to $B$, unlike in the preceding simultaneous-transformation proposition. The paper states this variant because it appears to hold numerically, but does not provide a proof.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.08813

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2019).
source_name: Tobias Damm and Heike Fassbender, “Simultaneous hollowisation, joint numerical range, and stabilization by noise”, arXiv:1910.08813 (2020).
